topic: domino tilings of a holed board
statement: An 8 x 8 chessboard has the 2 x 2 block of four squares at its center removed (the squares in rows 4-5 and columns 4-5). In how many ways can the remaining 60 squares be tiled by 30 dominoes, where each domino covers two squares that share an edge?

In how many ways can the 25 cells of a 5 x 5 grid be colored using the three colors red, green, and blue so that no two cells sharing an edge have the same color? Not every color needs to be used, and colorings that differ by a rotation or reflection of the grid count as different.

A 2 x 3 x 4 box is made of 24 unit cubes. In how many ways can it be completely filled by twelve 1 x 1 x 2 bricks, where each brick occupies two unit cubes that share a face (bricks may point in any of the three directions)?

Consider the complete graph on the vertices 1, 2, ..., 10. The edge {i, j} has weight w(i, j) = r - 3, where r is the remainder when i*j is divided by 7 (so every weight is an integer from -3 to 3). The weight of a perfect matching is the product of the weights of its five edges. Find the sum of the weights of all 945 perfect matchings of this graph.
How many permutations p of {1, 2, ..., 13} satisfy 1 <= |p(i) - i| <= 3 for every i in {1, 2, ..., 13}?

topic: gcd/lcm blackboard invariant (IMO 2026 P1 mechanics, new instance)
statement: Five numbers are written on a blackboard: 2^6 * 3^9, 2^9 * 5^6, 3^6 * 5^9 * 7^4, 2^15 * 7^6, and 3^12 * 7^10. A move consists of choosing two numbers m and n on the board that are both greater than 1, erasing them, and writing the two numbers gcd(m, n) and lcm(m, n)/gcd(m, n) in their place. Numbers equal to 1 stay on the board but can never be chosen. Moves are made until no move is possible. It turns out that at the end exactly one number greater than 1 remains, no matter which moves were made. What is that number?

topic: greedy gcd sequence (IMO 2026 P6 mechanics, new instance)
statement: Let a_1 = 35. For each n >= 1, let a_(n+1) be the smallest integer greater than a_n such that gcd(a_(n+1), a_i) > 1 for every i = 1, 2, ..., n. Find a_2026.
How many points (x, y, z) with integer coordinates satisfy x^2 + y^2 + z^2 <= 2026?

topic: Burnside on cube edges (full symmetry group)
statement: Each of the 12 edges of a cube is colored red, green, or blue so that exactly 4 edges have each color. Two colorings are considered the same if one can be carried to the other by a symmetry of the cube, where both rotations and reflections are allowed (48 symmetries in total). How many different colorings are there?

topic: random walk hitting time on 4x4x4 grid
statement: Consider the graph whose 64 vertices are the points (x, y, z) with x, y, z in {0, 1, 2, 3}, where two points are adjacent when they differ by exactly 1 in exactly one coordinate. A particle starts at (0, 0, 0) and each second moves to a neighbor of its current vertex chosen uniformly at random. The expected number of seconds until it first reaches (3, 3, 3) can be written as m/n in lowest terms. Find m + n.

Two players play a game with rows of coins. Initially there is a single row of n coins. A move consists of choosing one row and doing exactly one of the following: (a) removing one coin that is not at either end of that row, which splits the row into two nonempty rows; or (b) removing 2 or 3 consecutive coins from one end of that row (this removes the entire row if it has exactly 2 or 3 coins). Players alternate moves, and a player who cannot move loses. For how many integers n with 1 <= n <= 1000 does the second player have a winning strategy?

A bracelet consists of 15 beads equally spaced around a circle. Each bead is colored red, green, or blue, and no two adjacent beads have the same color. Two bracelets are considered the same if one can be obtained from the other by a rotation or a reflection. How many different bracelets are there?
